text: The reconstructed point acts on A⊗M by the original tensor-automorphism component. The source proves equality against every base-changed dual functional, using matrix-coefficient maps into finite regular subcomodules. This is the recovery step of [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). The base is a field, M is finite-dimensional, and A may be any commutative k-algebra. Checks pass: [fgPointTensorIso_reconstructedPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Equivalence.lean#L165), [eq_of_baseChange_matrixCoefficientHom_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L179).
Checks recovery of the full tensor automorphism.
Checks the separation mechanism after scalar extension.

The forward Tannakian equivalence sends g to its tensor action, exactly as in [Milne 9.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=177). The equation is definitional: packaging the proved bijective homomorphism changes neither the action nor convolution multiplication. The statement concerns a fixed commutative value algebra A over the field k, without asserting value-algebra naturality here. Checks pass: [reconstructedPoint_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L110), [fgPointTensorIso_reconstructedPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Equivalence.lean#L165).
Checks reconstruction after the forward map.
Checks the opposite round trip.

Reconstructing a point from η and taking its tensor action returns η. Naturality along finite matrix-coefficient morphisms identifies all scalar-extended dual evaluations; these separate vectors over the field, so every component agrees. This proves the surjectivity direction of [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), for commutative Hopf algebras, including those not finitely generated, and arbitrary commutative value algebras. Checks pass: [counit_baseChange_matrixCoefficientHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L155), [eq_of_baseChange_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L147).
Checks that counit evaluation recovers each dual functional.
Checks that all base-changed dual functionals separate tensors.

The inverse of the Tannakian equivalence is the explicitly reconstructed point. Although the equivalence constructor uses an abstract inverse to a bijection, the right-inverse identity uniquely identifies it with reconstruction. This matches [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); no choice of basis or finite subcomodule affects the resulting algebra-valued point. Checks pass: [fgPointTensorIso_reconstructedPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Equivalence.lean#L165), [reconstructedPoint_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L110).
Checks the right-inverse identity identifying the inverse.
Checks the left-inverse identity.

The compatible local functionals glue to a k-linear map H→A because finite regular subcomodules cover H over a field. Directedness makes their values agree on overlaps, as in [Milne’s proof of 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). The result is initially a linear functional; its unit and multiplication laws are proved separately. Checks pass: [globalFunctional_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L64), [globalFunctional_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L87).
Checks restriction to each finite regular subcomodule.
Checks that these restrictions determine the map.

A linear map agreeing with every extracted local functional equals the glued global functional. Every element of H belongs to a finite regular subcomodule, so the prescribed restrictions determine every value. This is the uniqueness part of [Milne’s gluing argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); finite means finite-dimensional here because the base is a field. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLift_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L168), [globalFunctional_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L64).
Checks the general uniqueness theorem used.
Checks the glued map has the required restrictions.

If η comes from an algebra-valued point g, its global functional is the underlying k-linear map of g. The local counit computation gives equality on every finite regular subcomodule, and coverage gives global equality. This implements evaluation at identity in [Milne 9.1–2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), retaining the point’s entire map H→A. Checks pass: [localFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L217), [reconstructedPoint_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L110).
Checks recovery on each finite regular subcomodule.
Checks the resulting algebra-valued point is also recovered.

The global functional sends 1_H to 1_A: choose a finite regular subcomodule containing 1, use the restriction formula, and apply the local unit law. This is the tensor-unit condition of [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175) propagated through gluing. Containment of 1 follows from the field-based finite-subcomodule theorem, not from every subcomodule being unital. Checks pass: [localFunctional_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Unit.lean#L165), [globalFunctional_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L64).
Checks the unit law on a subcomodule containing 1.
Checks restriction to that chosen subcomodule.

On any finite regular subcomodule N, the global functional has exactly the prescribed local value. This is the defining restriction property of the directed-union construction in [Milne’s proof of 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). The statement works for every N and every n∈N, making the value independent of which containing finite subcomodule is chosen. Checks pass: [globalFunctional_comp_subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L75), [localFunctional_eq_comp_inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L182).
Checks the same restriction as equality of linear maps.
Checks compatibility of the local data.

If all products from N and P lie in Q, their local functionals satisfy g_Q(np)=g_N(n)g_P(p). Naturality for multiplication, tensor compatibility and multiplicativity of the counit prove the identity, as in [Milne 9.2’s multiplication step](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). These are finitely generated subcomodules, not necessarily subalgebras; the containing-Q hypothesis is essential. Checks pass: [regularMulHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Multiplication.lean#L72), [scalarExtensionComponent_tensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L185).
Checks the multiplication morphism used for naturality.
Checks the tensor identity applied to the two inputs.

This packages n⊗p↦np as a comodule morphism N⊗P→Q, assuming every such product belongs to Q. Bialgebra compatibility makes multiplication colinear, matching [Milne 9.2’s equivariant multiplication](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176). The source permits noncommutative H; semiring Module.Flat means tensoring with H preserves injections, which supplies the inherited subcomodule coactions. Checks pass: [mulHom_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L111), [mulHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L120).
Checks the actual value on a pure tensor.
Checks the corestricted multiplication map.

Forgetting the categorical packaging of regular multiplication gives exactly the linear map underlying the corestricted multiplication N⊗P→Q. Thus no product order or codomain changes during bundling. It is the concrete map needed for [Milne’s equivariant-multiplication argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), under the explicit product-containment and semiring flatness hypotheses. Checks pass: [mulHom_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L111), [localFunctional_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Multiplication.lean#L120).
Checks the product order on pure tensors.
Checks use of that map in the local multiplicativity identity.

The reconstructed algebra-valued point evaluates at x as the glued global functional does. The source adds the proved unit and multiplication laws to that linear map, so its values are unchanged. This is the point recovered in [Milne 9.1–2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); WithConv changes the multiplication convention on points, not their underlying functions. Checks pass: [reconstructedPoint_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L102), [globalFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L116).
Checks the entire underlying linear map.
Checks the value when reconstruction starts from an actual point.

Starting with a point g, forming its tensor action and reconstructing returns g. The counit computation recovers its restrictions, and finite-subcomodule coverage recovers the whole linear map; algebra-map equality then follows. This is the uniqueness direction of [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), with no replacement of A-valued points by field-valued points. Checks pass: [globalFunctional_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L116), [fgPointTensorIso_reconstructedPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Equivalence.lean#L165).
Checks equality of the underlying linear maps.
Checks the other reconstruction direction.

To prove g(xy)=g(x)g(y), the source places x and y in finite regular subcomodules and finds a third containing all their products. The local tensor law then applies. This realizes [Milne 9.2’s multiplication argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); a finite subcomodule need not itself be multiplicatively closed, so the third object matters. Checks pass: [localFunctional_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Multiplication.lean#L120), [exists_finite_mul_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Multiplication.lean#L154).
Checks multiplicativity in a containing finite subcomodule.
Checks existence of that containing subcomodule under the actual freeness hypothesis.

The glued k-linear functional becomes a k-algebra homomorphism after its unit and multiplication laws are proved, yielding the reconstructed A-valued point of [Milne 9.1–2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). Linearity together with preservation of 1 ensures compatibility with k’s algebra map. WithConv equips these maps with convolution multiplication and leaves their evaluations unchanged. Checks pass: [globalFunctional_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L98), [globalFunctional_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L49), [reconstructedPoint_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L95).
Checks preservation of the unit.
Checks preservation of multiplication.
Checks the packaged point retains the global functional values.

Forgetting the algebra-homomorphism laws and convolution wrapper from the reconstructed point yields precisely the global functional. Equality of all values follows from its defining evaluation formula. This identifies the concrete functional used in [Milne’s reconstruction](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the construction does not modify the linear map when proving multiplicativity. Checks pass: [reconstructedPoint_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L95), [reconstructedPoint_fgPointTensorIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Reconstruction.lean#L110).
Checks equality on every element of H.
Checks recovery after starting with an actual point.

When N contains 1_H, its extracted functional sends that element to 1_A. Naturality along r↦r·1_H transfers the tensor-unit condition to N; counit evaluation then gives ε(1)=1. This is [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The containment hypothesis is explicit because a regular subcomodule need not contain the algebra unit. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionComponent_one_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Unit.lean#L124), [counitEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/LocalFunctional.lean#L78).
Checks the transported component fixes 1⊗1.
Checks the subsequent counit evaluation.

For a finite regular subcomodule containing 1, the tensor-automorphism component fixes 1⊗1. The source uses the comodule map from the trivial tensor unit into N and the automorphism’s naturality and unit law. This is the transported form of [Milne 9.2(b)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), rather than an assertion that the whole component on N is identity. Checks pass: [localFunctional_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Unit.lean#L165), [scalarExtensionComponent_tensorUnit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/Monoidal.lean#L366).
Checks the resulting local functional at 1.
Checks identity on the actual tensor-unit object.

Over a free coefficient coalgebra, a linear map is determined by its restrictions to all finitely generated subcomodules. The finite-subcomodule theorem covers every element, so equality is checked in one containing object. This is the uniqueness mechanism in [Milne’s directed-union argument](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), generalized here to semirings with the displayed freeness assumption. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLift_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L144), [globalFunctional_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L87).
Checks the glued map has the required restrictions.
Checks its application to the reconstructed global functional over a field.

A compatible family of linear maps on finite subcomodules glues to M→P, assuming explicitly that every element lies in one such subcomodule. Directedness gives agreement on overlaps and preserves addition. This is the gluing mechanism in [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); over these general semirings, coverage is a hypothesis rather than an automatic consequence. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLiftOfExistsMem_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L88), [finiteSubcomoduleLiftOfExistsMem_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L118).
Checks every local value is preserved.
Checks uniqueness and hence independence of the selected containing object.

The glued map evaluates an element of N by the prescribed map on N. The construction may choose another containing finite subcomodule, but directedness and inclusion compatibility force the same value. This matches the restriction equation in [Milne’s gluing proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176), under the explicit covering hypothesis; finite means finitely generated as an R-module. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLiftOfExistsMem_comp_subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L104), [finiteSubcomoduleLiftOfExistsMem_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L118).
Checks the full restriction identity.
Checks the local values characterize the global map.

This glues inclusion-compatible linear maps from all finite subcomodules when C is free over R. A basis expansion of the coaction supplies the finite-subcomodule covering, extending the field argument of [Milne 4.7–8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=97); the directed-union construction then gives a unique R-linear map. M itself need not be finite or free. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLift_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L144), [finiteSubcomoduleLift_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L168).
Checks the resulting restriction formula.
Checks uniqueness of the gluing.

The lift over a free coefficient coalgebra restricts to the assigned linear map on every finite subcomodule. Freeness supplies the covering theorem, while compatibility removes dependence on the containing object. This is the restriction property used in [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); the source states the broader semiring version with finite generation rather than finite dimension. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLift_comp_subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L156), [globalFunctional_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GlobalFunctional.lean#L64).
Checks equality of the restricted linear maps.
Checks the concrete Tannakian application.

Any linear map with the prescribed values on all finite subcomodules equals the glued map. For each m, the explicit covering hypothesis supplies a finite subcomodule containing it, where both maps agree. This is the uniqueness step behind [Milne 9.2](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=176); it needs no unasserted freeness or flatness of the coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [finiteSubcomoduleLiftOfExistsMem_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L88), [finiteSubcomoduleLift_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/DirectedUnion.lean#L168).
Checks the constructed lift has those values.
Checks the specialization when freeness supplies coverage.

For a nonzero finite nonnegative real r, taking its reciprocal and then including it in the extended nonnegative reals agrees with taking the extended reciprocal. The nonzero restriction matters: at r=0 the finite type defines the reciprocal as zero, whereas the extended type defines it as infinity. The inclusion cannot preserve both endpoint conventions. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L69).

Including a quotient of finite nonnegative reals in the extended type preserves division when the denominator is nonzero. The numerator may be zero. At a zero denominator the general rule fails: finite nonnegative arithmetic gives 1/0=0, while extended nonnegative arithmetic gives 1/0=∞. The hypothesis reconciles these different defaults on the ordinary domain. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L79).

Reciprocal reverses and reflects the order of all extended nonnegative values: a⁻¹≤b⁻¹ exactly when b≤a. Unlike the usual positive-real statement, no exclusions are needed here, because reciprocal exchanges zero and infinity. On positive finite values this is ordinary reciprocal order; at the endpoints, the greatest and least values exchange roles. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L303).

With a fixed extended nonnegative numerator c, increasing the denominator cannot increase the quotient: a≤b implies c/b≤c/a. This holds even when values are zero or infinity, using the stated reciprocal conventions. It asserts non-strict order only; for instance, a zero numerator gives zero for every denominator, so strict comparisons need not survive. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L472).

With a fixed extended nonnegative denominator c, increasing the numerator cannot decrease the quotient: a≤b implies a/c≤b/c. No denominator restriction is needed for this weak inequality. When c=∞ both quotients are zero; when c=0, positive numerators give infinity. These collapses explain why the theorem does not assert strict monotonicity. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L475).

For a positive finite denominator y, the inequality x/y≤z is equivalent to x≤z·y. The compared values x and z may themselves be zero or infinity; the restrictions concern only y. These are the ordinary nonnegative cross-multiplication rules, extended to infinite numerators or bounds while excluding denominator endpoints where cancellation can fail. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L238).

From a≤b·c one may conclude a/c≤b without assuming c is positive or finite. The endpoint cases explain this generality: if c=0, the premise forces a=0 and 0/0=0; if c=∞, the quotient is zero. Thus this one-way implication survives where an unrestricted cross-multiplication equivalence would fail. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L393).

A finite extended nonnegative numerator divided by a nonzero denominator has a finite quotient. The denominator may be infinity, in which case the quotient is zero; it need not be finite. These are sufficient conditions, not a complete characterization: even the excluded case 0/0 has the finite value zero under the totalized convention. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L215).

For positive finite a, the equation b=c/a is equivalent to a·b=c. Both b and c may be infinite, so only the denominator and multiplying factor a must avoid the endpoints. The result expresses reversible multiplication by a genuine positive finite scale; it does not license cancelling zero or infinity from arbitrary equations. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L518).

Given finite a and nonzero b in the extended nonnegative reals, some positive finite real multiplier makes its product with a smaller than b. The witness n is a nonnegative real, not a natural number; with a=b=1, one may take n=1/2. Zero a and infinite b are both allowed by the hypotheses. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L669).

Multiplying a value by a positive finite a and then by a⁻¹ recovers the original value: a⁻¹·(a·b)=b. The value b may be infinity. Only the cancelled factor must be nonzero and finite; at either endpoint a=0 or a=∞, the composite product becomes zero and cannot recover a nonzero b. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L122).

For positive finite x, the bound x⁻¹·y≤z is equivalent to y≤x·z. Multiplication by x reverses the effect of its reciprocal while preserving order. The values y and z may include zero or infinity; requiring only x to be positive and finite is enough for this equivalence and its cancellation step. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L230).

Multiplying a by a positive finite b and then dividing by b recovers a, including when a is infinity. The denominator b must be both nonzero and finite. If b is zero or infinity, the resulting quotient is zero, so the same cancellation claim would fail for every nonzero a. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L169).

The identity (a·b)/c=(a/c)·b holds for all extended nonnegative values, including zero and infinity. Division means multiplication by c⁻¹, so the equality only rearranges three factors using associativity and commutativity. It does not cancel c or require c to be invertible, which is why no denominator exclusions are necessary. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L195).

Reciprocal distributes over multiplication, (ab)⁻¹=a⁻¹b⁻¹, except when one factor is zero and the other infinity. Those two mixed endpoint pairs are excluded explicitly. They would give infinity on the left, since 0·∞=0, but zero on the right. Equal endpoint pairs, including (0,0) and (∞,∞), remain allowed. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L246).

For positive finite r, multiplying by r can be moved across a non-strict inequality as multiplication by its reciprocal: r·a≤b exactly when a≤r⁻¹·b. The compared values a and b may be infinite. The restrictions on r ensure both order reflection and cancellation; the statement does not assume all extended values have multiplicative inverses. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L484).

Division distributes over a sum in the numerator: (a+b)/c=a/c+b/c for all extended nonnegative values. Since division is multiplication by c⁻¹, this follows from multiplication distributing over addition. It includes c=∞, when all quotients are zero, and c=0, using zero for 0/0 and infinity for a nonzero numerator divided by zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L506).

Three copies of a/3 add back to a for every extended nonnegative value. The denominator is the ordinary positive finite number three, so finite inputs obey the usual thirds identity. Zero contributes three zeros, while an infinite input contributes three infinities whose sum is infinity. No finiteness assumption on a is needed. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L544).

Applying reciprocal twice recovers every extended nonnegative value, including zero and infinity because these endpoints are exchanged. For positive finite values this is the usual reciprocal identity. The claim concerns an involutive function, not multiplicative invertibility of every value: zero still satisfies 0·0⁻¹=0 rather than 1 under the extended arithmetic convention. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L198).

The multiplicative monoid carries reciprocal, division a/b=a·b⁻¹, and integer powers formed from natural powers and reciprocal, with 1⁻¹=1. For extended nonnegative reals, reciprocal exchanges zero and infinity. This structure packages these operations and identities; it does not make every element invertible or grant unrestricted cancellation, since 0·0⁻¹=0. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L90).

Every uncountable Borel subset s of a Polish space contains a continuous injective image of {0,1}^ℕ with its product topology. Compactness of this domain and the Hausdorff target make it a homeomorphic Cantor copy. The Borel-space assumption makes “measurable” mean Borel; continuity is for the original topology. See [Tserunyan, Introduction to Descriptive Set Theory, Corollary12.5 and Theorem12.1, p.46](https://www.math.mcgill.ca/atserunyan/Teaching_notes/dst_lectures.pdf). The required [irrationals-in-[0,1] Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Examples/MeasureTheory/PerfectSet.lean#L29) passes.
The constructed Cantor injection gives exact continuum cardinality

A subset s of a Polish space is a countable intersection of open sets exactly when s, with the inherited topology, admits a complete compatible metric and is separable. This includes the empty subset. Completeness concerns some compatible metric; the ambient metric restricted to s need not be complete. See [Tserunyan, Theorem1.11 and Lemma1.10, pp.6–7](https://www.math.mcgill.ca/atserunyan/Teaching_notes/dst_lectures.pdf). Native checks pass: [complete-metric construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Topology/MetricSpace/PolishGDelta.lean#L102) and [subspace converse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Topology/MetricSpace/PolishGDelta.lean#L119).
The forward construction supplies a complete compatible metric
A completely metrizable subspace is Gδ
